devdoc.details: If cooldown duration is set to zero, the StakedPikuV2 behavior changes to follow ERC4626 standard and disables cooldownShares and cooldownAssets methods. If cooldown duration is greater than zero, the ERC4626 withdrawal and redeem functions are disabled, breaking the ERC4626 standard, and enabling the cooldownShares and the cooldownAssets functions.

DelegationError().details: thrown when attempting to delegate more votes than an address has free, or exceeding the max delegates

UndelegationVoteError().details: thrown when attempting to undelegate more votes than the delegatee has unused.

Approval(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when the allowance of a `spender` for an `owner` is set by a call to {approve}. `value` is the new allowance.

DelegateChanged(address,address,address).details: this is used for backward compatibility with OZ interfaces for ERC20Votes and ERC20VotesComp.

DelegateVotesChanged(address,uint256,uin.details: Emitted when a token transfer or delegate change results in changes to an account's voting power.

Delegation(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when a `delegator` delegates `amount` votes to `delegate`.

EIP712DomainChanged().details: MAY be emitted to signal that the domain could have changed.

RoleAdminChanged(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32.details: Emitted when `newAdminRole` is set as ``role``'s admin role, replacing `previousAdminRole` `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is the starting admin for all roles, despite {RoleAdminChanged} not being emitted signaling this. _Available since v3.1._

RoleGranted(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is granted `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call, an admin role bearer except when using {AccessControl-_setupRole}.

RoleRevoked(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is revoked `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call:   - if using `revokeRole`, it is the admin role bearer   - if using `renounceRole`, it is the role bearer (i.e. `account`)

Transfer(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when `value` tokens are moved from one account (`from`) to another (`to`). Note that `value` may be zero.

Undelegation(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when a `delegator` undelegates `amount` votes from `delegate`.

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `amount` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

params._asset: The address of the PIKU token.
params.initialRewarder: The address of the initial rewarder.
params.owner: The address of the admin role.

address to redeem and start cooldown, owner must allowed caller to perform this action

decimals().details: Necessary because both ERC20 (from ERC20Permit) and ERC4626 declare decimals()

decreaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically decreases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `spender` must have allowance for the caller of at least `subtractedValue`.

delegate(address).details: undefined for `delegateCount(msg.sender) > 1` NOTE This is meant for backward compatibility with the `ERC20Votes` and `ERC20VotesComp` interfaces from OpenZeppelin.

params.delegator: the account which is delegating votes to delegates.
the account which is delegating votes to delegates.
the account which is delegating votes to `delegatee`.

the address to get votes of.

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

params.account: the address to get votes of.

increaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically increases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

incrementDelegation(address,uint256).details: requires "freeVotes(msg.sender) > amount" and will not exceed max delegates

mint(uint256,address).details: See {IERC4626-mint}. As opposed to {deposit}, minting is allowed even if the vault is in a state where the price of a share is zero. In this case, the shares will be minted without requiring any assets to be deposited.

name().details: Returns the name of the token.

owner().details: Necessary because both SingleAdminAccessControl and Ownable declare owner()

redistributeLockedAmount(address,address.details: Burns the full restricted user amount and mints to the desired owner address.

params.from: The address to burn the entire balance, with the FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKER_ROLE
params.to: The address to mint the entire balance of "from" parameter.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Remove renounce role access from AccessControl, to prevent users to resign roles.

params.amount: The amount of tokens to be rescued.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.

params.amount: the amount of votes taken away.

params.receiver: Address to send the assets by the staker

userdoc.notice: The StakedPikuV2 contract allows users to stake PIKU tokens and earn a portion of protocol LST and perpetual yield that is allocated to stakers by the Ethena DAO governance voted yield distribution algorithm.  The algorithm seeks to balance the stability of the protocol by funding the protocol's insurance fund, DAO activities, and rewarding stakers with a portion of the protocol's yield.
